# pikopod

> pikopod is an open-source sandbox for the third-party APIs you depend on. Built from the provider's spec, it fails on purpose: rehearsal scenarios run against a deterministic sandbox before you ship, and when production fails anyway, the incident replays into the same sandbox so you fix it on a laptop and keep the fix as a test.

pikopod is a command-line tool written in Go. It builds an offline sandbox from a provider's OpenAPI spec or docs URL, wraps webhooks, and runs failure-rehearsal scenarios (declines, timeouts, retry storms, rate limits, duplicate deliveries) that a real provider never lets you practice on. `pikopod spec-diff --fail-on` gates CI when a provider's spec drifts, and `pikopod replay` turns a captured production incident into a passing regression test. Licensed under Apache-2.0.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Pikopod/pikopod/blob/main/README.md): full feature overview, quickstart, and CLI reference.
- [Installation](https://github.com/Pikopod/pikopod#quickstart): `go install github.com/Pikopod/pikopod@latest` and the basic import / up / run loop.
- [Scenario guide](https://github.com/Pikopod/pikopod#scenarios): writing failure-rehearsal scenarios, standing state, and binding to real endpoints.
- [CI integration](https://github.com/Pikopod/pikopod#ci): gating with `spec-diff --fail-on`, exit codes, and the `--ci` replay flag.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/Pikopod/pikopod/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): releases and notable changes.
